column2: The Register-based censuses 2011 and 2021 and the annual Register-based labour market statistics (since 2012) are complete surveys on characteristics of the Austrian resident population as per 31 October and are conducted by using information from administrative registers. The characteristics and definitions are based on the EU regulation on population and housing censuses. For further information see (German only): https://www.statistik.at/fileadmin/shared/QM/Standarddokumentationen/B_1/std_b_abgestimmte_erwerbsstatistik.pdf This database contains the results for all persons with a usual residence (resident population). The data from 2021 onwards can be found here: https://statcube.at/statcube/opendatabase?id=deaest_aest_zr_personen .) Territorial structure of 2024. .) Updating: annual update of the territorial structure last update: [2026-06-09] Highest level of education attained 2015 revised, 2011-2014 not revised. .) For analyses based on very small cell values, no reliable assertions can be made.

In order to guarantee protection of data privacy, persons with a third sex category are not separately reported. They are imputed either as "male" or "female".

A family nucleus consists of couples (married or cohabiting) with or without children, or parents with one or more children living in the household. According to family statistics, all biological children, step children and adopted children, who do not have an own partner and have no child of their own while still living in the household of their parents are regarded as children, regardless of their age. Married couple: Both partners are married according their de jure marital status. Includes registered partnerships. Consensual union couple: Neither are both partners married nor in a registered partnership according to her/his de jure marital status. One-parent family: Fathers/Mothers living with children but without partner.
Private households according to the household dwelling concept.
